By Advs. Sri. Ajith Viswanathan, Government Pleader Sri. Anwin John Antony This Writ Petition (Civil) Having Been Finally Heard On 22.05.2025, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following: W.P.(C)No.37538 of 2024 :3: 2025:Ker:35216 Judgment
texts.facts: Dated this the 22nd day of May, 2025 The petitioner states that he has taken a shop building from the 3rd respondent on oral lease and is running a hotel business, taking registration from FSSAI. According to the petitioner, he is in possession of the shop building for more than nine months. Respondents 2 and 3 are now trying to forcefully evict him. They have even used JCB for demolishing the building. 2. When this writ petition came up for admission, this Court passed an interim order on 25.10.2024, whereunder police protection was granted to the petitioner and his family members. Counsel entered appearance on behalf of respondents 2 and 3 and resisted the writ petition. Respondents 2 and 3 submitted that they have not granted the shop room on lease to the petitioner. There is no piece of paper to establish the same.
texts.arguments: The contention of the petitioner before this Court is that he is in possession of the building as per an oral lease from the 3rd respondent. In fact, in the petitioner's complaint before the police, the petitioner submitted that he was taken the building on lease from Mr. Tejus C.T. That itself would show that the petitioner has committed fraud and is creating fraudulent documents. As the petitioner is in illegal possession, the petitioner cannot seek police protection to perpetuate the illegality. 4.
